SecurityPool

Exposes question shares and reporting. Standalone pools also hold ETH settlement collateral and REP underwriting and account for vaults and fees. SecurityPool source contract

Read surface

Relationship and configuration getters, all set at construction, are questionId, universeId, initialEscalationGameDepositAttoRep, zoltar, parent, shareToken, repToken, openOraclePriceCoordinator, openOracle, escalationGameFactory, eventEmitter, questionData, securityPoolForker, truthAuction, securityPoolFactory, and statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps; the current game is escalationGame. The start bond is derived at construction from live universe theoretical REP supply rather than copied from factory configuration. Accounting getters include totalUnderwritingLimitAttoEth, settlementCollateralAttoEth, totalRepBackingUnits, shareTokenSupplyAttoShares, securityVaults, minimumSecurityBondDebtAttoEth, minimumVaultRepDepositAttoRep, totalBadDebtAttoEth, and vaultBadDebtAttoEth. For standalone pools, aggregate and per-vault bad debt describe only the current collateral-claim generation; getPoolAccountingSnapshot exposes its badDebtGeneration. Exhausting the standalone claim supply clears aggregate debt and advances the generation before later collateral can be minted. Portfolio redemption uses its central settlement book and does not advance this native generation. Use getVaultUnderwritingLimitAttoEth for the standing owner-authorized ETH commitment, separate from REP deposits. Use getVaultCapacityBackingFactorsBps for current associated and pool-held REP-per-capacity ratios and getVaultOpenInterestAttoEth for a vault’s live proportional obligation. getCurrentMintingCapacityAttoEth returns zero once an escalation game exists; otherwise it returns total standing commitments for a standalone pool, or the question’s checkpointed settlement collateral plus available shared minting capacity for a portfolio-bound pool. Other derived and paged reads are getVaultCount, getVaults, attoSharesToAttoEth, attoEthToAttoShares, attoRepToBackingUnits, backingUnitsToAttoRep, getTotalPoolHeldAttoRep, totalAccruedFeesAttoEth, getPoolAccountingSnapshot, getFeeEpochEndTime, getVaultFeeRemainder, and isEscalationResolved. The backing-factor ratios are not current vault health: associated REP includes only the game’s eligible retained dispute collateral as at-risk security, while current health also depends on the full underwriting commitment, REP-per-ETH price, the security multiplier, and both protocol constraints. The native vault registry is append-only and newest-registered first; it does not enumerate portfolio owners. Registration requires only a nonzero address and can occur without economic state; consumers filter current positions from securityVaults, escalation stake, and bad debt. isEscalationResolved() is true when the pool inherits a fixed fork outcome, or when a local escalation game is configured and the forker routes a non-None outcome. An operational fixed-outcome child remains available for settlement and redemption but rejects new collateralized operations. getFeeEpochEndTime() returns the native fee-epoch cutoff, or type(uint256).max for an open standalone child epoch. A resolved standalone child without a continuation game fixes that cutoff at activation. Portfolio fees follow the central stream’s cutoff. Lifecycle and fee getters are totalClaimableVaultFeesAttoEth, lastUpdatedFeeAccumulator, feeIndex, currentRetentionRate, awaitingForkContinuation, and systemState. Portfolio-bound pools expose portfolioCustody as their capital ledger. The native linearFeePrincipalAttoEth, linearFeeRateAttoEthPerSecond, portfolioFeeRateAttoEthPerSecond and linearFeeEndTime fields are not synchronized central fee inputs; read principal, rate and end from the central settlement book, and owner positions from the capital ledger. Accounted central REP excludes unsolicited token donations.

Security assumptions

Price-sensitive withdrawal, commitment-increase, and liquidation calls depend on A16 timely inclusion, A21 genesis REP and WETH behavior, A19 observable correctable price, and A06 lifecycle executors. User-initiated pool calls additionally depend on A28 account authority.

State-changing interactions

Each call lists its parameter names in ABI order. The contract index defines the columns. When portfolioCustody is nonzero, it names the central capital ledger: provider deposits, commitments, health targets, retirement and liquidation use that ledger, while native per-vault REP backing deposits, commitment changes, splits and liquidation reject. The central settlement book owns question cash and fees; only native share supply, settlement cash and the last checkpoint timestamp mirror it. Native vault and fee fields do not describe bound owner positions or central fee streams. Reporter REP uses separate central custody. Portfolio minting accepts only its registered purchase route and enforces fresh aggregate healthy capacity. A resumed bound continuation accepts wallet reports on an unrelated unresolved question; a fixed outcome rejects new reports. Legacy vault-funded reporting and native per-question fork exports are unavailable for bound pools. Rows marked "through fallback()" are not in the compiled ABI: the pool forwards exactly those four selectors to SecurityPoolOperationsDelegate by delegatecall and rejects every other unknown selector with Unsupported pool operation.

Transaction Caller Main prerequisites State or asset effect Primary signals
setPortfolioCustody(custody) The canonical portfolio registered by the factory Nonzero custody, not previously bound, with no existing backing units or commitment. The caller must match the factory portfolio namespace. Binds the portfolio’s central capital ledger once and registers central question cash and fee accounting. The native pool holds no provider principal for this path. Due accounting checkpoints and fee-stream replacement
creditEscalationSurplus(amountAttoRep) The active escalation game Caller equals the configured game; transfer precedes this callback. For standalone pools, credits irrevocable ordinary surplus to backing, or burns it when no backing units exist. For bound pools, transfers surplus to the portfolio for vested provider earnings; reporter principal remains separate. Portfolio accounting callback, or REP burn when ownerless; the game emits the source accrual event
creditEscalationAuctionBacking(amountAttoRep) The active escalation game Caller is the configured game; any recorded incoming backing cannot exceed the actual token balance. Checkpoints authenticated incoming auction REP. Standalone pools need no separately accounted balance; bound reporter custody does not use per-question auction exports. Accounting callback when bound
creditForkBacking(amountAttoRep) The canonical forker Caller is the configured forker; any recorded incoming backing cannot exceed the actual token balance. Checkpoints authenticated incoming fork REP. Standalone pools need no separately accounted balance; portfolio fork principal migrates through its central ledger. Accounting callback when bound
refreshPortfolioFees() Anyone The fee rate and end fit the fixed stream key widths; any increased budget is funded from question collateral. Checkpoints earned fees and replaces a bound question’s funded prospective linear stream using central fee principal, the configured annual fee and cutoff. A forked universe only checkpoints its sealed book. No-op for standalone pools. Due accounting checkpoints and fee-stream replacement
splitVaultPosition(recipient, numerator, denominator) Vault owner Standalone pool (Use shared capital ledger otherwise); recipient is nonzero and differs from the caller (Invalid position recipient); 0 < numerator <= denominator (Invalid position fraction). Its onSecurityPoolVaultPositionReceived(source) callback must return that callback’s selector (Position not accepted). After the callback, the pool must be operational or forked (Pool inactive) and the caller must have no dispute-staked REP (Source has dispute escrow). Checkpoints both vaults, then moves the requested fraction of the caller’s REP backing units, underwriting commitment, current-generation bad debt, claimable fees, and fractional fee carry to recipient. Each component rounds down; the caller keeps the remainder. No REP or ETH is transferred, and total backing, commitment, and bad debt are unchanged. Combining fee carry can make another whole attoETH claimable from the unallocated fee reserve, or from settlement collateral when the pool is forked. Fee and vault checkpoints when due; VaultPositionSplit, then VaultAccountingCheckpoint for each vault and PoolAccountingCheckpoint
burnEscalationWinnerHaircut(amountAttoRep) This pool's EscalationGame only Caller is the configured escalation game; amount is positive and the game has already transferred enough REP to the pool. Burns REP the game has just transferred to the pool: a winning deposit's escalation haircut, or any game’s terminal residual. RepBurned and ERC-20 Transfer; child REP also emits Burn
setUnderwritingLimit(limitAttoEth) Vault owner Standalone, operational pool (Pool inactive) in an unforked universe (Forked); a resolved operational pool may still reduce a commitment after an unrelated late fork. Increases require open admission, a fresh price (Stale price), and both full-commitment backing checks (Vault backing insufficient). Before final resolution, reductions must leave total commitments at least equal to tracked settlement collateral (Commitments below collateral). With a concrete final outcome, reductions may reach zero while shares remain outstanding; their ETH collateral stays reserved. Checkpoints the vault fees, then changes the underwriting commitment independently of REP ownership and recalculates retention. A call that repeats the current value returns before the checkpoint and changes nothing. Fee-accrual and retention-change PoolAccountingCheckpoint events when due; then UnderwritingLimitSet, VaultAccountingCheckpoint, and PoolAccountingCheckpoint; no event for a call that repeats the current value
setVaultUnderwritingLimit(vault, limitAttoEth) through fallback() This pool's VaultOperations executor only (Unauthorized) The setUnderwritingLimit prerequisites, evaluated for vault. Applies the setUnderwritingLimit change to vault. The executor calls it for a coordinator SetVaultUnderwritingLimit operation and for the commitment change in a vault bundle. The setUnderwritingLimit signals, with UnderwritingLimitSet naming vault
depositRepToVault(amountAttoRep, targetHealthFactorBps) Vault owner Standalone, operational and unforked; isEscalationResolved() is false; the transaction timestamp is strictly before the question end time unless the pool has an inherited fork-continuation game; amountAttoRep is positive (Zero REP); targetHealthFactorBps is at least statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps (Target below pool minimum); resulting vault REP is at least minimumVaultRepDepositAttoRep (Vault REP below minimum). targetHealthFactorBps is only checked against that floor; it neither is stored nor authorizes a commitment. Checkpoints the vault fees, prices proportional REP backing units before receiving the transfer, pulls amountAttoRep from the caller through the caller's allowance to this pool, then credits only those units. Depositing REP never changes the underwriting commitment. Fee-accrual checkpoints when due; REP Transfer; RepDepositedToVault, VaultAccountingCheckpoint, then PoolAccountingCheckpoint
depositRepToVaultWithPermit(amountAttoRep, targetHealthFactorBps, deadline, v, r, s) through fallback() Vault owner The pool universe is not genesis (Genesis REP does not support permit); the permit succeeds or the caller allowance to this pool is at least amountAttoRep (Vault permit and allowance insufficient); the depositRepToVault prerequisites. Calls the REP token permit for amountAttoRep from the caller to this pool, ignores a failed permit when the existing allowance already covers the amount, then performs the depositRepToVault deposit. REP Approval when the permit succeeds, then the depositRepToVault signals
depositRepToVaultWithAuthorization(owner, amountAttoRep, targetHealthFactorBps, validAfter, validBefore, nonce, v, r, s) through fallback() Anyone relaying the owner's ERC-3009 signature The pool universe is not genesis (Genesis REP does not support authorization); the depositRepToVault prerequisites for owner; the signature authorizes the token nonce keccak256(abi.encode(nonce, operationHash, owner)), where operationHash is keccak256(abi.encode(depositRepToVaultWithAuthorization.selector, owner, universeId, questionId, amountAttoRep, targetHealthFactorBps)). Runs the depositRepToVault checks for owner, pulls amountAttoRep from owner to this pool through the REP token receiveWithAuthorization, then credits owner's vault. Fee-accrual checkpoints when due; REP AuthorizationUsed and Transfer; RepDepositedToVault, VaultAccountingCheckpoint, then PoolAccountingCheckpoint
depositRepToVaultFromExecutor(owner, amountAttoRep) through fallback() This pool's VaultOperations executor only (Only vault operations executor) The depositRepToVault prerequisites for owner, other than the target check, which always passes. Performs the depositRepToVault deposit for owner, pulling REP through owner's allowance to this pool, with the target fixed at statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps. The depositRepToVault signals
redeemFees(vault) Anyone; any nonzero ETH payment is always sent to vault A nonzero payment path requires vault to accept ETH. First accrues the vault's fees. If resulting claimable fees are zero, returns without payment; otherwise clears and pays the full amount. Accrual checkpoints only when accrual state changes; both VaultAccountingCheckpoint and PoolAccountingCheckpoint for a nonzero redemption; no event when fees and accrual state are unchanged
createCompleteSet() with ETH Anyone for a standalone pool; only the registered portfolio purchase helper for a bound pool Operational and unforked; timestamp before question end (Question ended otherwise); no escalation game, pending continuation, or inherited fixed outcome; positive ETH converts to at least one complete-set unit. Standalone resulting collateral must not exceed native standing commitments, without a price or REP backing check at mint. Bound minting requires the active authorized portfolio purchase and fresh aggregate healthy capacity for increased central demand; the native commitment ceiling does not apply. A contract share recipient must accept onERC1155BatchReceived under A22 asset-recipient compatibility. Mints one Invalid, Yes, and No share per complete-set unit to the direct caller. Standalone pools retain the ETH as native settlement collateral; bound pools forward it into the central settlement book. A contract caller receives the ERC-1155 batch-receiver callback; rejection rolls back the transaction. The portfolio purchase route subsequently forwards the minted shares to its selected recipient. Accrual PoolAccountingCheckpoint when due; CompleteSetCreated, PoolAccountingCheckpoint, then ERC-1155 TransferBatch on a successful callback; standalone retention PoolAccountingCheckpoint when the rate changes; bound minting additionally emits central settlement and fee-stream checkpoints
redeemCompleteSet(amountAttoShares) Anyone; positive redemption requires the caller to hold the complete set Operational and unforked; caller holds every requested outcome amount. A standalone caller must accept the ETH call even at zero; a bound caller need only accept a positive central cash payout. Zero shares require no token balance. Burns equal balances of all three outcomes. Standalone pools pay amountAttoShares * settlementCollateralAttoEth / shareTokenSupplyAttoShares, rounded down, from native collateral; exhausting their economic claim supply clears native bad debt and advances its generation. Bound pools convert burned outcome shares into question settlement units, then those units into cash from the applicable live or protected final book, rounding down at each conversion; full redemption consumes the remaining units or cash at that step. They update the central book and mirrored question balances without advancing native bad-debt generation. Zero shares still follow outer token, event and checkpoint processing: standalone pools make a zero-value ETH call; bound pools skip the central redemption and payment. Bound cash payouts of zero also make no ETH call. CompleteSetRedeemed and PoolAccountingCheckpoint
redeemShares() Anyone; a positive payout requires the caller to hold winning shares Operational pool with a final outcome. A standalone caller must accept the ETH call even at zero; a bound caller need only accept a positive central cash payout. Burns the caller’s full winning balance. Standalone pools pay the downward-rounded fraction of native collateral and clear native bad debt when the remaining economic share supply reaches zero. Bound pools use the same outcome-share-to-settlement-unit-to-cash conversion and rounding as redeemCompleteSet, with the central book paying the caller; native bad-debt generation is unchanged. A zero winning balance still follows outer token, event and checkpoint processing, but only standalone pools make a zero-value ETH call. Bound cash payouts of zero also make no ETH call. SharesRedeemed and PoolAccountingCheckpoint
redeemRepFromVault(vault) Vault owner; caller must equal vault, and REP is sent to vault Operational pool with a final outcome; the specified vault has no remaining escalation escrow, has positive backing units, and has exited its underwriting commitment by setting it to zero (Exit commitment before REP redemption) under the limit-reduction rules. First settles an ordinary final game, preserving winner liabilities and burning terminal surplus. Burns the vault's REP backing units and returns its proportional vault REP backing; zero-valued units can be retired without a token transfer. Ordinary settlement signals when applicable; fee-accrual checkpoints when due; REP Transfer only for positive REP, then RepRedeemedFromVault and VaultAccountingCheckpoint
depositWalletRepToEscalationGame(outcome, maximumDepositAttoRep) REP holder with a token allowance for the pool Question end time reached (block.timestamp >= endTime) before starting a game; pool operational in an unforked universe, without an inherited fixed outcome or pending fork continuation; a standalone game is not a fork continuation, while a bound game may be a resumed unrelated continuation; outcome and amount accepted; sufficient wallet REP and pool allowance. No existing vault or oracle price is required. Starts an ordinary game if needed and transfers the accepted REP from the caller to the game. Standalone escrow remains at the game; a bound game forwards it into its separate central reporter ledger. Records the caller as depositor without minting vault backing units or underwriting commitments. Also accepts deposits if another reporter has already started the ordinary game. GameStarted, then EscalationGameSet, when the call deploys the game; REP Transfer; game LocalDepositAppended and DepositOnOutcome; game NonDecisionReached when the deposit reaches non-decision
depositToEscalationGame(outcome, maximumDepositAttoRep) Vault owner Standalone pool only (Use wallet-funded reporter REP otherwise). Question end time reached (block.timestamp >= endTime); pool operational in an unforked universe, without an inherited fixed outcome, and not awaiting continuation. On the first deposit, the live non-decision threshold must exceed one attoREP; outcome and amount accepted; the remaining vault and aggregate pool totals each preserve both full-commitment backing requirements; the vault keeps either no REP or at least minimumVaultRepDepositAttoRep (Vault REP below minimum); a fresh price is required when total underwriting commitment is nonzero. Deploys the local game on the first deposit. The game factory uses the configured start bond while it is below the live non-decision threshold; if tracked REP supply later makes it too large, the factory uses nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep - 1 instead. Repeat deposits use the existing game's stored startBondAttoRep and nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep. Every accepted deposit removes enough REP backing units and escrows dispute-staked REP on the selected outcome. GameStarted, then EscalationGameSet, when the call deploys the game; REP Transfer; game LocalDepositAppended and DepositOnOutcome; game NonDecisionReached when the deposit reaches non-decision; then DepositToEscalationGame and VaultAccountingCheckpoint
withdrawFromEscalationGame(outcome, depositIndexes) Anyone; a nonempty list must select deposits belonging to one original depositor Game configured; operational pool; valid final outcome. If an external fork interrupted the game, parent withdrawal stays unavailable (Migrate deposits first): winners settle in the child by carried proof, inherited losers require no transaction, and unresolved parent escalation-deposit accounting cleanup is optional. A nonempty list additionally requires valid local indexes and one common depositor. A nonempty list settles local deposits and pays winning REP to the immutable depositor recorded by each deposit. Liquidation cannot change that payout address. An empty list returns after the outer lifecycle checks without settlement, state change, or event. Per processed deposit, escalation-game CarryDepositConsumed and VaultEscrowUpdated; additionally ClaimDeposit for a winning deposit. No event for an empty list
withdrawForkedEscalationDeposits(outcome, proofs) Anyone; a nonempty list must name one original depositor across all proofs Game configured; operational child pool; valid final outcome. A nonempty list additionally requires an initialized and fully resumed continuation game, valid unconsumed winning proofs, and one common depositor. A nonempty list verifies and consumes carried proofs, then pays winning child REP to the immutable depositor committed in each leaf. Stable continuation identities retain the creating game. Standalone allocations apply source-game auction removals through bounded checkpoint preparation. Central reporter allocations keep identity coordinates across live forks and require no ancestor traversal. An empty list returns after the outer lifecycle checks without proof verification, state change, or event. Per processed proof, escalation-game CarryDepositConsumed and ClaimDeposit. No event for an empty list
updateSettlementCollateral() Anyone No caller restriction. Standalone accrual returns when its accumulator is already at or beyond the clamped timestamp, while still caching the fee-epoch cutoff. Bound pools use the central checkpoint, including snapshot-only reads of a sealed fork book. Portfolio-bound pools checkpoint central fee and finality accounting, then mirror the question’s share supply, settlement cash and logical timestamp into the native pool. Standalone pools accrue fees through their effective fee-epoch cutoff: for an initial pool, question end applies while its universe remains unforked; if its question remains unresolved when the universe forks, the fork timestamp replaces question end, including a later question-end-to-fork interval. A question finalized before the fork retains its question-end cutoff. Finalizing an activated standalone child starts a separate epoch at that timestamp, running until the child game resolves or its universe forks. An inherited fixed-outcome child without a continuation game accrues no fees after finalization. Standalone accrual moves whole credited fees from collateral into the unallocated accrued-fee reserve and advances the accumulator without charging an interval twice. With positive elapsed time but zero fee-eligible commitment it clears denominator-specific remainder and advances the timestamp without charging fees. Bound pools: central fee/finality events when due, and PoolAccountingCheckpoint only if the mirrored timestamp changes. Standalone pools: PoolAccountingCheckpoint when positive elapsed time is processed, including zero-commitment accrual; no event for an unchanged timestamp
updateRetentionRate() Anyone No caller restriction. The bound-pool branch runs before the native lifecycle check. Standalone pools return unless Operational; otherwise they first accrue fees and store a changed rate. Zero standalone minting capacity, including an existing escalation game, selects maximum retention. Portfolio-bound pools call refreshPortfolioFees() to checkpoint central accounting and refresh the prospective linear fee stream; a forked universe only checkpoints its sealed book. Standalone pools recalculate the retention curve from current collateral and live minting capacity. Bound pools: central fee/finality events when due and FeeStreamReplaced when the stream is refreshed. Standalone pools: accrual PoolAccountingCheckpoint when due, plus another checkpoint only if the stored retention rate changes
updateVaultFees(vault) Anyone for any address No caller, nonzero-vault, or lifecycle restriction. First checkpoints pool accounting. For a bound pool’s portfolioCustody address, only its native fee index is synchronized; no native vault is registered or fee claim assigned. For other addresses, advances the native vault fee index and fractional remainder, moves whole assigned fees from reserve to the vault, registers any previously unseen nonzero vault address regardless of economic state, and returns leftover reserve to settlement collateral once a forked pool has checkpointed all fee-eligible underwriting commitment. It never changes an underwriting commitment, including in an empty pool. Accrual PoolAccountingCheckpoint when due. The bound custody-address branch emits no additional checkpoint. Other addresses emit VaultAccountingCheckpoint when the native vault index, remainder, or claimable fee balance changes; an additional PoolAccountingCheckpoint when pool accounting changes; no event when neither accrual nor vault or pool accounting changes
withdrawRepFromVault(vault, amountAttoRep) This pool's VaultOperations executor only (Unauthorized) Fresh coordinator price; operational pool in an unforked universe; isEscalationResolved() is false; no vault REP escrow. The remaining vault backing must meet both upward-rounded associated-REP and pool-held-REP requirements for its full underwriting commitment, with equality healthy. The remaining aggregate backing must also cover the entire total underwriting commitment under both backing constraints. A withdrawal cannot implicitly exit a commitment. Removes the requested proportional REP backing units, or all backing units when the requested remainder would fall below the REP minimum; preserves the vault and aggregate underwriting commitments; recalculates retention; and transfers the resulting withdrawable REP to vault. REP Transfer; RepWithdrawnFromVault; VaultAccountingCheckpoint; and applicable fee-accrual or retention PoolAccountingCheckpoint events
performLiquidation(request) This pool's VaultOperations executor only (Unauthorized) Standalone pool only (Use shared capital ledger otherwise). In ABI order, request contains operationId, operator, receiverVault, targetVault, requestedDebtAttoEth, snapshot, minimumReceiverHealthFactorBps, and minLiquidationPriceDistanceBps. The nested snapshot contains only targetBackingUnits and targetUnderwritingLimitAttoEth. Fresh settled coordinator price; operational pool in an unforked universe; isEscalationResolved() is false; receiver differs from target; neither participant has current-generation bad debt. A bad-debt-bearing vault becomes eligible again after the current collateral claims are exhausted, which clears aggregate debt and advances the bad-debt generation. The two target snapshot fields must match, while execution reads current pool totals. After target and receiver fee checkpoints, the liquidation delegate requires live target backing, dispute-staked REP, and full underwriting commitment to remain at least minLiquidationPriceDistanceBps beyond the liquidation threshold and requires the live target state to remain unhealthy. When debt moves, the receiver must satisfy the protocol backing checks multiplied by its approved minimum health factor, using live post-liquidation state and upward-rounded requirements; its resulting commitment must meet the configured debt floor and its REP must meet the vault floor. The target resulting commitment must be zero or meet the commitment floor; partial awards reserve the target REP floor when available. Transfers up to the requested ETH commitment from target to authorized receiver, conserving total commitments. REP awards are capped by available target backing. A sufficiently backed receiver can accept the full commitment even when the nominal award is underfunded. Fees checkpoint first and remain with their earners; escalation claims remain with their owners. Residual commitments remain visible and continue earning fees. Liquidation creates no write-off. Fee-accrual checkpoints when due; VaultLiquidated only when a positive commitment moves, identifying operation, operator, receiver, and target, with the moved commitment in both securityBondDebtMovedAttoEth and underwritingLimitMovedAttoEth and zero badDebtAttoEth; target VaultAccountingCheckpoint always; receiver VaultAccountingCheckpoint only when a positive commitment moves; then PoolAccountingCheckpoint
setStartingParams(currentRetentionRate, settlementCollateralAttoEth) SecurityPoolFactory only Caller is the factory (Only factory). The pool has no internal one-shot or lifecycle guard; the factory exposes it only through atomic deployment wiring. Sets the fee timestamp and initial question-end epoch cutoff, retention, and collateral, seeds the coordinator with zero for an origin or the parent's last price for a child, then checkpoints initialization. Coordinator RepEthPriceSet and CoordinatorStateCheckpoint, then pool PoolAccountingCheckpoint, even for zero or repeated values if the factory were to call again
activateForkMode() SecurityPoolForker only No inherited fixed outcome and no direct current-state guard. A bound pool requires a forked, prepared source universe when first freezing its central books. A standalone configured game must permit its drain or activation reverts. Portfolio-bound pools freeze their universe’s central capital, settlement and reporter books, then mark this question PoolForked; branch settlement owns asset migration. Standalone pools set PoolForked, accrue through the fork clamp, transfer all pool-held REP to the forker and drain the configured escalation game to it. Repeated standalone calls transfer replenished balances and repeat the checkpoints. Bound pools: due central checkpoints and ForkFrozen on the first universe freeze. Standalone pools: pool-held REP Transfer including zero, positive configured-game REP Transfer, accrual checkpoint when due, then PoolForkModeActivated and fork-activation PoolAccountingCheckpoint
initializeForkedEscalationGame(startBondAttoRep, nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep, elapsedAtFork, fixedQuestionOutcome) SecurityPoolForker only No game is configured (otherwise it reverts without reason data); downstream startFromFork parameters are valid. Deploys and starts the pool's paused fork-continuation game with inherited timing and optional fixed outcome, and reopens vault admission after question end. Escalation GameContinuedFromFork, then pool EscalationGameSet
initializeForkCarryOutcome(sourceGame, snapshotId, peaks, leafCount, carryTotalAttoRep, resolutionBalanceAttoRep, nullifierRoot) SecurityPoolForker only A game is configured; it is a fork continuation with fewer than three initialized outcomes; leaf counts fit the MMR; every call supplies the same source and nonzero snapshot ID, with the next outcome’s data; the third call verifies the full commitment. Installs the next outcome of the continuation game’s canonical snapshot. Three calls complete its immutable carry peaks, counts, totals, resolution balances, and normalized nullifier roots. ForkCarryCheckpoint on completion of the third outcome
resumeForkedEscalationGame() Anyone Pool is operational, awaiting a configured fork continuation, and the game has not resumed. The carry snapshot is complete and funded; a bound game additionally requires its fixed response period to have started. Checks aggregate REP funding of the installed carry commitment and clears the pool wait flag after resumption. Standalone games start their remaining escalation clock at the transaction timestamp. Bound games retain the branch’s fixed response anchor, so late materialization does not extend their clock. ForkContinuationResumed and AwaitingForkContinuationSet(false)
setAwaitingForkContinuation(shouldAwait) SecurityPoolForker only No lifecycle or value-change guard. Stores whether complete-set minting must wait for continuation initialization, then refreshes bound portfolio fee accounting. AwaitingForkContinuationSet, including for a repeated value; bound pools then emit central checkpoints and stream replacement when applicable
setSystemState(newState) SecurityPoolForker only No transition or value-change guard. Replaces the pool lifecycle state directly, then refreshes bound portfolio fee accounting. SystemStateSet, including for a repeated state; bound pools then emit central checkpoints and stream replacement when applicable
configureVault(vault, repBackingUnits, underwritingLimitAttoEth, vaultFeeIndex, newVaultBadDebtAttoEth, newTotalBadDebtAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only vault is nonzero; no lifecycle or value-change guard. Replaces the vault REP backing units, price-independent underwriting commitment, fee index, vault bad debt, and aggregate pool bad debt, clears pooled fee-index remainder when underwriting commitment changes, and registers the nonzero vault address regardless of the supplied state. Always VaultAccountingCheckpoint and PoolAccountingCheckpoint, including when all supplied values repeat current state
activateRecoveredCommitment(vault, commitmentAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only Operational, unforked pool, fresh price and both backing checks on the receiver’s entire resulting underwriting commitment. Activates prospective fee eligibility for an orphaned commitment after the forker checkpoints and assigns its backing and commitment. Total commitments remain unchanged. PoolAccountingCheckpoint
configureFinalizedAuctionVault(vault, repBackingUnits, underwritingLimitAttoEth, vaultFeeIndex, newVaultBadDebtAttoEth, newTotalBadDebtAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only vault is nonzero; the forker has already included the sold underwriting commitment in the pool fee denominator at auction finalization. Assigns finalized-auction REP backing and already-fee-eligible underwriting commitment to the winning vault without clearing the pool-wide fee-index remainder, then replaces the vault fee index, bad debt, and aggregate pool bad debt and registers the vault. Always VaultAccountingCheckpoint and PoolAccountingCheckpoint, including when all supplied values repeat current state
setTotalRepBackingUnits(newTotalRepBackingUnits) SecurityPoolForker only No lifecycle or value-change guard. Replaces the REP backing units denominator. TotalRepBackingUnitsSet, including for zero or a repeated value
setShareTokenSupplyAttoShares(newShareTokenSupplyAttoShares) SecurityPoolForker only No lifecycle or value-change guard. Replaces stored shareTokenSupplyAttoShares, the standalone collateral denominator. Bound share conversion and redemption use the central settlement book, whose checkpoint refreshes this mirrored field. ShareTokenSupplySet, including for zero or a repeated value
setPoolFinancials(newSettlementCollateralAttoEth, newTotalUnderwritingLimitAttoEth, newFeeEligibleUnderwritingLimitAttoEth, newTotalBadDebtAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only Fee-eligible underwriting commitment does not exceed total underwriting commitment. Actual ETH covers the supplied collateral plus all accrued fee liabilities. Installing inherited liabilities does not require current REP solvency. Installs native standalone child finances: settlement collateral, both underwriting-commitment totals and aggregate bad debt; resets the fee timestamp, opens the finalized child native epoch unless its outcome is fixed without a continuation game, and clears fee-index rounding carry. It does not install portfolio liabilities or fee terms. Its final bound fee refresh restores cash, share supply and timestamp mirrors from the authoritative central book. PoolAccountingCheckpoint, including for repeated financial values
authorizeChildPool(pool) SecurityPoolForker only This parent pool is already authorized; candidate reports this share token; candidate universe has no different canonical pool. No pool-lifecycle guard. Asks the lineage share token to establish pool as the canonical authorized pool for its universe; reauthorizing the same pool is a no-op. AuthorizationUpdated only on first authorization; no event when already authorized
transferEth(receiver, amountAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only Fee liabilities are covered; amountAttoEth fits both unreserved pool ETH and tracked settlement collateral; receiver accepts the ETH call, including zero value. Reduces tracked settlement collateral by amountAttoEth, checkpoints the reconciliation, and calls receiver with that ETH. At zero amount it reduces no settlement collateral but still emits the checkpoint and performs a zero-value call; callback rejection rolls back the transaction and checkpoint. PoolAccountingCheckpoint, including at zero amount; no dedicated ETH-transfer event
assignFinalizedAuctionFees(vault, amountAttoRep, auctionFeeIndexAtFinalization) SecurityPoolForker only Despite its name, amountAttoRep is the claimed underwriting commitment in attoETH: the pool uses it as the fee weight and subtracts it from its uncheckpointed fee-eligible commitment. The supplied finalization index does not exceed the current fee index (Fee index); the forker credit workflow has already checkpointed the vault and added the claimed underwriting commitment. Assigns to the claiming vault the fees its auctioned underwriting commitment accrued from Truth Auction finalization through the current fee index, combines fractional carry with the vault remainder, and removes whole assigned fees from the unallocated reserve. The ownership was already included in the fee denominator and total ownership at finalization. This call preserves aggregate fees and settlement collateral; after every eligible ownership is reconciled on a forked pool, a subsequent permissionless updateVaultFees checkpoint returns any reserve that no vault can individually claim to settlement collateral. VaultAccountingCheckpoint and auction-claim PoolAccountingCheckpoint; the calling forker emits ClaimAuctionProceeds only after the broader credit workflow completes
Direct ETH transfer to receive() Anyone for a bound pool; only its forker, Truth Auction or parent for a standalone pool (Bad ETH sender) The standalone sender must be one of the three authorized protocol addresses. Bound pools have no sender restriction. Forced ETH bypasses this ordinary-call guard. Accepts direct ETH and emits its receipt. This function does not credit settlement collateral or fees; standalone migration and auction workflows account for their routed ETH separately. Direct donations to a bound native pool do not fund its central settlement book. Forced ETH also remains unaccounted. EthReceived identifies the sender and amount received; forced ETH bypasses receive() and emits no such event

Accounting examples

Retention rate and annualized fee

SecurityPoolUtils.calculateRetentionRate returns a per-second retention factor scaled by PRICE_PRECISION (1e18). It equals MAX_RETENTION_RATE at zero utilization, declines linearly until utilization reaches RETENTION_RATE_DIP (80% of minting capacity, which is total underwriting commitments outside an escalation game), and stays at MIN_RETENTION_RATE above that. Zero minting capacity selects MAX_RETENTION_RATE.

  • MAX_RETENTION_RATE = 999_999_996_848_000_000, about a 9.5% yearly fee.
  • MIN_RETENTION_RATE = 999_999_977_880_000_000, about a 50.2% yearly fee.

Clients annualize a retention rate for display as follows; the contract never computes this value.

annualFee=1−(retentionRatePRICE_PRECISION)SECONDS_PER_YEAR

Liquidation transfer rounding

A liquidation request bounds the underwriting commitment transferred, capped by the target’s underwriting commitment. The nominal REP award includes LIQUIDATION_REP_BONUS_BPS = 500 (5%). REP and backing units round upward before the award is capped at available units. The receiver is checked against its entire resulting underwriting commitment and backing-unit position. Total underwriting commitments remain constant, including at zero settlement collateral. Target claims and earned fees remain with their owners.

No liquidation writes off a commitment. An untransferred residual stays visible and continues earning fees. A fully backed receiver can accept the target’s entire underwriting commitment even when the nominal REP award is not fully funded. Partial transfers reserve available target REP for the minimum balance, and the remaining commitment must be zero or meet the commitment floor.
